test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 03 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: I bought two bicycles for ₹1,200. I sold the first one at a loss of 8% and the second at a gain of 17%. If, on the whole I made neither a loss nor a gain, find the cost price (in ₹) of the first bicycle.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the **method of allegation**, the loss on the first bicycle is 8% and the gain on the second is 17%.

Since there is **no profit and no loss**, the overall profit/loss percentage is 0%.

Ratio of CP₁ : CP₂ = (17 − 0) : (0 − (−8)) = 17 : 8.

Total units = 17 + 8 = 25 units. Given 25 units = ’1,200.

Cost price of the first bicycle = (17 ÷ 25) × 1,200 = 17 × 48 = 816.

**∴ The correct answer is ’816.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Total CP = ’1,200 | Loss₁% = 8% | Gain₂% = 17% | Total Profit = 0.
Formulas: Profit = SP − CP | Loss = CP − SP | Total Profit/Loss = (P₁/L₁) + (P₂/L₂).
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/28acda6160136c6175b6038b33bf5d85d3c9f74fdac9773a467e96747a07367c.png] 
⇒ Let the cost price of the first bicycle be **x** and the second be (1,200 − x).
⇒ Loss on first = 8% of x = 0.08x.
⇒ Gain on second = 17% of (1,200 − x) = 0.17 × (1,200 − x).
⇒ Since net profit is zero: 0.08x = 0.17 × (1,200 − x).
⇒ 0.08x = 204 − 0.17x ⇒ 0.25x = 204.
⇒ x = 204 ÷ 0.25 = 816.

**∴ The correct answer is ’816.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

No Profit No Loss Condition

This occurs when the absolute value of loss on one item equals the absolute value of profit on the other. **CP₁ × L₁% = CP₂ × P₂%**.

Allegation Method

A faster way to find the ratio of quantities (or cost prices) when two components are mixed to reach a mean value.</p
